name: App archiving and offloading
plain: Both systems can remove an unused app but keep its data, so a reinstall restores the old state.
meaning: Android 15 archiving and iOS Offload Unused Apps free storage while keeping user data. A later reinstall looks like a returning user, not a new one.

android.persistence: User data kept; app restored from the store
android.store_policy: Play Store auto-archive supported on Android 15
android.note: Archived app keeps a launcher icon with an archived mark; installer must support unarchive

ios.prompt_ui: Settings > App Store > Offload Unused Apps
ios.persistence: Documents and data kept; app binary removed
ios.api_surface: ApplicationStatus, no API for the app to detect offload
ios.note: Triggers automatically when storage is low if enabled; app data stays until deleted

limits.headline: Can remove an unused app but keep your data so a reinstall brings it back
limits.user_action: You tap Archive or Offload Unused Apps, or the phone does it when storage is low
can: Keep your app data after the app itself is removed
Keep the icon on the home screen, marked as archived or offloaded
Restore your old state when you tap the icon again
cannot: Keep running; an archived or offloaded app does nothing until restored
Restore on Android unless the store that installed it supports unarchive
Keep data once you delete the app fully
limits.reach_label: Data stays, the app is gone
limits.differs: iPhone calls it Offload and can do it automatically when storage is low. Android calls it Archive in Android 15.

story.what_it_is: Removes an unused app to free space but keeps your data so a reinstall picks up where you left off.

marketing.name: Offload Unused Apps
marketing.pitch: Apple lets iPhone remove unused apps and keep documents and data so you can reinstall later.

marketing.name: App archiving
marketing.pitch: Android 15 adds archiving to free storage while keeping user data.

story.for_you: An app you have not opened in months goes grey with a small cloud icon. Tap it and it comes back with your old data. Nothing is lost.
story.for_makers: Makers see a returning user, not a new one, when the app is restored. Their servers must handle this quietly and keep sign in working.

use_cases.example: A big game you left for months comes back with your progress.
A streaming app returns with your downloads list and profile.
A notes app returns with your offline notes intact.
A shopping app returns with your saved cart and login.
A product team must tell archived and restored users apart from real new installs.
An attribution tool must avoid counting a restore as a new install.
A fitness app returns with years of workout history.

risks: Restore can look like a new install
story.android_note: Archived apps keep an icon with an archived mark. The installer must support unarchive.
story.ios_note: Offload Unused Apps can start on its own when storage is low.

technical_bounds: The app cannot detect it ran offloaded
Android relies on the store as installer
